title: ConformanceCase
description: One case in the component conformance corpus: a sequence of calls with their expected results, run through every binding the component supports and required to produce identical results. This is the mechanism that makes 'built-ins implement exactly these interfaces' a fact rather than an intention (ADR 0012 decision 4). A case that can only be expressed in one binding is not a case — it is a report that the interface has split. See spec.md §9.4.

name.description: Stable identifier for the case, used in failure output.

interface.description: Which interface the case exercises, when it exercises one.

bindings.description: Bindings this case must run through. Absent means every binding the component supports — which is the normal case and the point of the corpus.

Expected.title: Expected
Expected.description: What the call must produce, carrying exactly one of 'ok' or 'error'. Results are compared after canonicalisation; members the case does not mention are not constrained, so a case does not break when a result grows a member additively.

error.description: Expected error. A case asserting an error asserts its 'code'; 'message' is never asserted.
